Oil was found at Seria, on the coast of Brunei, in 1929 by a company of the Shell group. Production began in the 1930s, and the field remains one of the largest in the region.

Oil and later natural gas turned a poor protectorate into one of the richest states per person in Asia. Revenue pays for free schooling and health care, no income tax and the wealth of the royal family.

The oil fields were seized by Japan in 1941 and set on fire as it retreated. Oil also made Brunei unwilling to share its wealth by joining Malaysia in 1963, after the Brunei revolt. See also British protection.
